item.title: DXC in advanced talks to sell insurance software unit for $2.4 billion, sources say
item.description: IT services company DXC Technology is in advanced talks to sell its insurance software and services division to private investment firm Eldridge Industries for about $2.4 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn
item.content:encoded: IT services company DXC Technology (DXC.N) is in advanced talks to sell its insurance software and services division to private investment firm Eldridge Industries for about $2.4 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Eldridge is discussing combining the business with Zinnia, its insurance technology platform that provides software and digital infrastructure to life insurance and annuity providers, the sources said. An agreement could be reached in the coming weeks, although there is no certainty a deal will be finalized, the people said, requesting anonymity because the discussions are confidential. DXC Technology, Eldridge and Zinnia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

item.title: Amazon diz que chips próprios de IA serão compatíveis com PyTorch
item.description: A Amazon.com está lançando uma nova ferramenta que permite que seus microprocessadores de inteligência artificial personalizados executem códigos baseados na biblioteca de programação de IA PyTorch, sem necessidade de modificações.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Nellis
item.content:encoded: A Amazon.com (AMZN.O) está lançando uma nova ferramenta que permite que seus microprocessadores de inteligência artificial personalizados executem códigos baseados na biblioteca de programação de IA PyTorch, sem necessidade de modificações. As ações da empresa subiram 5% nas negociações da manhã desta segunda-feira, com o Morgan Stanley classificando a ação da Amazon como “top pick”. O TorchNeuron permite que programadores executem código escrito com a PyTorch nos chips de IA Trainium da Amazon com uma única alteração de configuração e sem a necessidade de reescrever programas, de acordo com a unidade de chips Annapurna Labs da Amazon. A Amazon, que planeja anunciar o software em uma conferência de desenvolvedores no Vale do Silício nesta segunda-feira, afirmou que a ferramenta será lançada publicamente como uma oferta gratuita e de código aberto. O PyTorch, a biblioteca de código aberto apoiada pela Meta (META.O) , é usado pela maioria dos programadores de IA. A Nvidia dedicou mais de uma década à sua ferramenta de software chamada Cuda, que faz com que o PyTorch funcione bem nos chips da Nvidia. Outras empresas de computação em nuvem, como o Google (GOOGL.O) , que também possui seus próprios chips de IA personalizados, estão trabalhando para atrair desenvolvedores da Nvidia com ferramentas melhores para a PyTorch. Colin Brace, vice-presidente de software da Annapurna Labs, disse que a iniciativa visa reduzir o número de etapas que os desenvolvedores de IA precisam seguir para testar os chips desenvolvidos internamente pela Amazon. “O objetivo tem sido atender aos clientes onde eles estão”, disse ele à Reuters em uma entrevista. Brace disse que mais de 30 dos primeiros clientes, abrangendo robótica, modelos mundiais e IA de voz, estão usando o novo software, e que a migração para os chips da Amazon pode resultar em uma economia significativa de custos.

item.title: Flick clarifies Barcelona backline options before PSG and Real Madrid showdowns
item.description: Hansi Flick has confirmed that Raphinha could return to Barcelona's starting XI against Paris St Germain on Tuesday in the Champions League, amid a defensive injury crisis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hansi Flick has confirmed that Raphinha could return to Barcelona's starting XI against Paris St Germain on Tuesday in the Champions League, amid a defensive injury crisis. The Catalan club lost both Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia to injury on Sunday, leaving them with just five fit senior defenders. Raphinha could make first start for Barcelona since September 19 after hamstring issue. Garcia, Kounde and Andreas Christensen will all miss blockbuster PSG clash through injury. Flick says Kounde will be back "soon" and could play against Real Madrid on Sunday. Midfielders Rodri Hernandez and Frenkie de Jong cited by Flick as makeshift options for backline. Teenage centre back Alex Campos in squad for PSG game. The 18-year-old has yet to make Barcelona debut.

item.title: S&P Global advierte de que es probable que "hiperescaladores" tengan más deuda de la que se conoce
item.description: S&P Global dijo que es probable que las mayores empresas tecnológicas del mundo tengan más pasivos relacionados con la inteligencia artificial (IA) de lo que se conoce, pero su principal analista del sector no ve necesidad de modificar ninguna calificación por el momento.
item.dc:creator: Marc Jones
item.content:encoded: S&P Global dijo que es probable que las mayores empresas tecnológicas del mundo tengan más pasivos relacionados con la inteligencia artificial (IA) de lo que se conoce, pero su principal analista del sector no ve necesidad de modificar ninguna calificación por el momento. La calidad de la deuda emitida por los proveedores de infraestructura de IA y las llamadas empresas "neocloud", como CoreWeave —respaldada por Nvidia—, ha caído a niveles cada vez más críticos en las últimas semanas, en un escenario de preocupación por la magnitud de su endeudamiento. Mark Habib, director global de Infraestructura Digital de S&P, dijo que el mayor riesgo para las calificaciones de los hiperescaladores sigue siendo que los beneficios previstos no se materialicen. Sin embargo, también destacó las denominadas "estructuras de financiación interconectadas", en las que los hiperescaladores garantizan de hecho la construcción de enormes centros de datos o el funcionamiento de empresas de IA más pequeñas. "Es seguro suponer que hay más (deuda) ahí fuera que no estamos viendo", dijo Habib durante una mesa redonda celebrada en Londres. "Si no se declara, entonces no forma parte de la información facilitada por los hiperescaladores. Además, si no calificamos las transacciones en las que puede devengarse este pasivo, lo cierto es que es posible que no tengamos visibilidad al respecto". S&P prevé que los seis principales hiperescaladores estadounidenses —Amazon (AMZN.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Oracle (ORCL.N) , Meta (META.O) y SpaceX (SPCX.O) — gasten más de 7 billones de dólares en centros de datos y otras inversiones de capital relacionadas con la IA entre 2025 y 2030, y que tengan un flujo de caja libre negativo al menos hasta el año que viene. Habib señaló que no existía una estimación de cuánta deuda más podría suponer la financiación circular para los balances de las empresas, pero añadió que S&P estaba tratando de adoptar una visión "holística".

item.title: US Supreme Court seeks government's input on Iowa immigration arrest law
item.description: The US Supreme Court on Monday asked President Donald Trump's administration to weigh in on whether it should review a lower court ruling that blocked an Iowa law allowing state officials to arrest and prosecute people who are in the United States illegally.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Wiessner
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court on Monday asked President Donald Trump's administration to weigh in on whether it should review a lower court ruling that blocked an Iowa law allowing state officials to arrest and prosecute people who are in the United States illegally. Iowa is appealing [USN:L2N3OK0TE TEXT:"an 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals decision"] that said the Republican-led state's 2024 law interferes with federal immigration enforcement The law makes it a crime to enter Iowa for anyone who has been previously deported or denied entry to the United States The Supreme Court asked for the US Solicitor General's views on whether it should take the case brought by advocacy group Iowa Migrant Movement for Justice and two state residents who had previously been deported or otherwise removed from the US but were allowed to reenter as lawful permanent residents Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird's office says that the law supplements federal enforcement and plaintiffs lack standing to sue Former President Joe Biden's administration [USN:L1N3IG0HE TEXT:"sued Iowa"], Texas and other states for passing immigration enforcement laws The Trump administration has supported the states' efforts The case is Bird v. Iowa Migrant Movement for Justice, US Supreme Court, No. 26-49. item.title: WTA roundup: Lilli Tagger ousts Liudmila Samsonova in Osaka opener
item.description: Austria's Lilli Tagger improved to 2-0 this year against Liudmila Samsonova of Russia with a 6-3, 6-3 upset of the No. 5 seed in the first round of the Japan Open on Monday in Osaka.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Austria's Lilli Tagger improved to 2-0 this year against Liudmila Samsonova of Russia with a 6-3, 6-3 upset of the No. 5 seed in the first round of the Japan Open on Monday in Osaka. Tagger converted all three break points while not facing any on her serve, finishing with more than twice as many winners as unforced errors (19-9) in the 72-minute victory. It wasn't the only upset of the day, as Ashlyn Krueger ousted sixth-seeded Janice Tjen of Indonesia 6-4, 6-4. Krueger came away with the only breaks of the match at 4-4 in the first set and 3-3 in the second, winning 81% of her first-serve points and 80% of her second-serve points. No. 4 Talia Gibson of Australia was the only seeded competitor to win her opener Monday, edging Great Britain's Harriet Dart 7-5, 7-6 (6). Austria's Sinja Kraus was leading 6-4, 3-1, when Caty McNally retired. Lanlanna Tararudee of Thailand and Switzerland's Viktorija Golubic also won in straight sets, while eighth-seeded Brit Katie Boulter led 6-3, 3-1 over Japan's Himeno Sakatsume when play was suspended due to rain. Ningbo Open Leylah Fernandez of Canada rallied for a 2-6, 6-3, 7-5 defeat of seventh-seeded Belgian Elise Mertens in a first-round match in China. Fernandez overcame a sloppy performance, which saw her pair one ace with 11 double faults and 28 winners with 42 unforced errors. She saved seven of 14 break points while converting seven of 12 in the 2-hour, 49-minute battle. No. 8 seed Sorana Cirstea of Romania, the only other seeded competitor in action, swept China's Han Shi 6-3, 6-2. Alexandra Eala of the Philippines beat France's Diane Parry 6-3, 6-1 and Czech Marie Bouzkova beat Kamilla Rakhimova of Uzbekistan 6-4, 6-4 to set up a second-round match against No. 2 seed Iga Swiatek of Poland. Belarus' Aliaksandra Sasnovich bested Australia's Daria Kasatkina 6-4, 6-2. --Field Level Media

item.title: Acciones europeas caen ante deterioro de confianza provocado por disturbios en Francia
item.description: Las acciones francesas registraron el lunes su peor jornada en casi dos semanas tras los disturbios que estallaron en varias ciudades del país durante el fin de semana, lo que lastró a las bolsas europeas.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: Las acciones francesas registraron el lunes su peor jornada en casi dos semanas tras los disturbios que estallaron en varias ciudades del país durante el fin de semana, lo que lastró a las bolsas europeas. * El índice de valores CAC 40 (.FCHI) de Francia cayó un 1,1%, mientras que el índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 (.STOXX) retrocedió un 0,9%, a 639,1 puntos. * Las protestas, provocadas por el aumento de los precios y el deterioro de los servicios públicos, han empañado la confianza de los inversores hacia un país que ya se enfrenta a un crecimiento débil y a una deuda creciente. * La agitación en la segunda economía más grande de la zona del euro, que se suma a la incertidumbre política de cara a las elecciones presidenciales de 2027, también ha sido en parte responsable de que el índice STOXX 600 se haya mantenido estancado en un estrecho rango durante el último mes. * Las entidades bancarias francesas BNP Paribas (BNPP.PA) , Société Générale (SOGN.PA) y Crédit Agricole (CAGR.PA) registraron caídas de entre el 2,5% y el 3,4%. La cadena minorista Carrefour (CARR.PA) bajó un 2,2% y el operador de centros comerciales Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield (URW.PA) cedió un 2%. * La incertidumbre política también cobró protagonismo en España, donde el índice bursátil de referencia (.IBEX) cayó un 1,5%. Las elecciones anticipadas previstas para el próximo mes han generado recelo entre los inversores. * Los partidos de extrema izquierda españoles presentaron el sábado listas de candidatos independientes para las elecciones, lo que reduce las posibilidades del presidente del Gobierno, el socialista Pedro Sánchez, de mantenerse en el poder al frente de una coalición de izquierdas. * Los sectores cíclicos lideraron las caídas en toda Europa, siendo los bancos (.SX7E) los que más se resintieron con un descenso del 2,2%. Las acciones del sector de la defensa (.SXPARO) también se vieron sometidas a presión, con una caída del 1,5%. * El índice tecnológico (.SX8P) se mantuvo en terreno positivo, con un alza del 0,7%. La semana pasada, las acciones europeas resistieron mejor que sus homólogas estadounidenses durante una ola de ventas en los valores relacionados con la inteligencia artificial, provocada por la preocupación ante el aumento de la deuda para financiar el gasto en infraestructuras. * Entre los valores que más han destacado, Barclays (BARC.L) cayó un 3,5%, alcanzando su nivel más bajo desde mediados de junio. * El Banco de Inglaterra investiga si los operadores de Barclays falsearon la información sobre préstamos de crédito privado ilíquidos para subestimar su riesgo, después de que una fuente interna del banco británico expresó su preocupación, informó el Financial Times, citando a personas familiarizadas con el asunto.

item.title: Bonfires of electric bikes burn in Paris riots
item.description: As protests rock France, the sight of electric bikes burning has become commonplace in the unrest.
item.dc:creator: Ronan Corcoran
item.content:encoded: As [USN:L1N4650EF TEXT:"protests rock France"], the sight of electric bikes burning has become commonplace in the unrest. In Paris, black smoke and flames rose over piles of the e-bikes at the weekend. Elsewhere in the city, a protester threw an e-bike onto a burning car. Shared-mobility operator Dott said in a statement to Reuters on Monday that about 300 of its electric bikes were destroyed and 120 severely damaged in Paris during the [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"nationwide protests"] on Saturday, which turned violent in several cities. It has 6,000 bikes in the city. The company also said 80 vehicles, including bikes and scooters, were destroyed in Bordeaux and 30 to 40 scooters in Lyon. It estimated the damage at around €400,000 ($450,000). Lime said some of its shared bicycles and scooters in Paris were destroyed or damaged during the protests, with the company losing about 6% of its Paris fleet. Ahead of the demonstrations, Lime said it worked with police to remove vehicles from designated protest routes and restricted parking and riding in several high-risk areas, adjusting those measures over the weekend as the situation evolved. Velib, whose bikes are docked, rather than parked on pavements, said in a report in Le Parisien newspaper that around 5% of its fleet of 18,000 e-bikes was destroyed or damaged at the weekend. It did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters. E-bikes often use lithium-ion batteries, which can ignite and produce intense fires that spread rapidly and produce toxic smoke. There was no indication that e-bike operators were specifically targeted during the protests over the cost of living and underfunded public services that have [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"descended into riots and looting"]. However, with thousands of bicycles available across Paris streets and docking stations, they proved readily accessible to protesters, with many used to build barricades or to set on fire.

item.title: Senators coach Travis Green signs multi-year extension
item.description: The Ottawa Senators signed head coach Travis Green to a multi-year contract extension on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Ottawa Senators signed head coach Travis Green to a multi-year contract extension on Monday. Four other members of the coaching staff also received extensions with Ottawa off to a 6-3-0 start this season. Green, 55, is 95-60-18 with two playoff berths since taking over in May 2024. The extension keeps him in the Canadian capital through the end of the 2030-31 campaign. "When I was in the search to identify our head coach two years ago, it was clear to me that Travis had the qualities to move our team forward. I have watched him implement systems and structures that have reinforced my belief in his coaching abilities," said Steve Staios, Senators president of hockey operations and general manager. "We share the same vision and philosophy and are confident we can continue to build on our team." Assistants Nolan Baumgartner, Ben Sexton and Mike Yeo and goaltending coach Justin Peters also received multi-year extensions. Green owns a career record of 236-219-53 including stints with the Vancouver Canucks (2017-21) and as interim coach of the New Jersey Devils in 2024. --Field Level Media

item.title: Aumenta contratación de empresas de servicios petroleros en Venezuela en primera oleada inversiones
item.description: Empresas de servicios petroleros como Weatherford International, Baker Hughes, Halliburton y SLB están ofreciendo decenas de nuevos puestos de trabajo en Venezuela, según portales de empleo, en una señal de que el plan de Washington de reconstruir la industria energética del país empieza a tomar forma.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney, Marianna Parraga
item.content:encoded: Empresas de servicios petroleros como Weatherford International, Baker Hughes, Halliburton y SLB están ofreciendo decenas de nuevos puestos de trabajo en Venezuela, según portales de empleo, en una señal de que el plan de Washington de reconstruir la industria energética del país empieza a tomar forma. La contratación, que podría ayudar a revertir el éxodo de empresas y profesionales que se produjo durante la era de las sanciones, forma parte de los esfuerzos del Gobierno de Donald Trump por impulsar 100.000 millones de dólares en inversiones para el país tras la captura de Nicolás Maduro en enero. Mientras algunos grandes productores indican que necesitan estabilidad política y reglas jurídicas claras antes de comprometer grandes inversiones, muchas firmas internacionales de servicios petroleros están dando los primeros pasos para desplegar personal y equipos especializados en el terreno. Weatherford (WFRD.O) , que había reducido al mínimo su presencia en Venezuela en 2019, tiene al menos 20 vacantes abiertas -de supervisores de operaciones, especialistas en perforación, soldadores, ingenieros y personal para el área de ventas, entre otros- desde el mes pasado principalmente para los centros de operaciones de petróleo y gas de Anaco y Maturín. La compañía estadounidense tiene previsto celebrar un evento este mes junto a Eni (ENI.MI) tras un acuerdo clave alcanzado en septiembre con la estatal PDVSA que permitirá a la petrolera italiana expandir operaciones en la Faja del Orinoco, dijo una fuente, que agregó que Eni está negociando una alianza con Weatherford para el proyecto. Weatherford y Eni no respondieron a solicitudes de comentarios. Baker Hughes (BKR.O) , que también se está expandiendo, tiene actualmente una docena de vacantes publicadas en su sitio web para puestos en Maracaibo, la segunda mayor región petrolera de Venezuela. La empresa firmó este mes un acuerdo clave con PDVSA, la firma de ingeniería Lindsayca y la desarrolladora Fulcrum LNG para reactivar infraestructura de gas en Venezuela. Por su parte, SLB (SLB.N) tiene 35 vacantes en oferta en su sitio web para puestos en Anaco, Maturín y Caracas publicadas en los últimos seis meses. A principios de octubre, Halliburton (HAL.N) hizo pública su intención de ampliar su red de talento en Venezuela. Un portavoz de Baker Hughes dijo que la empresa no hace comentarios sobre su personal. SLB declinó comentar, mientras que Halliburton no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Las ofertas de empleo representan una oportunidad para que profesionales venezolanos en el extranjero regresen al país, mientras que el personal que está trabajando en Venezuela podría negociar salarios más altos. La mayoría de las empresas extranjeras de servicios petroleros habían cerrado o reducido operaciones en Venezuela tras la imposición de sanciones por parte de Estados Unidos en 2019, lo que conllevó al despido o transferencia de personal, así como al retiro de equipos del país. EQUIPOS EN CAMINO Taladros y equipo especializado para los campos petroleros también están comenzando a hacerse visibles, aunque comenzando desde un nivel muy bajo. Según datos de Baker Hughes, este mes solo había dos taladros de perforación activos en Venezuela. Equipos estadounidenses de segunda mano, incluidas decenas de taladros para reacondicionamiento de pozos -muchos de ellos adquiridos en subastas- han estado ingresando al país este año. La firma North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP), que cuenta con respaldo estadounidense, informó que la semana pasada recibió dos unidades de perforación. Por su parte, se espera que Chevron (CVX.N) active pronto cuatro equipos. Patterson-UTI , uno de los mayores contratistas de perforación de Estados Unidos, está enviando componentes para 10 viejos equipos. Según su director ejecutivo, Andy Hendricks, se trata de un tipo de taladro que la empresa no ha utilizado en Estados Unidos desde hace unos 15 años. "Para Venezuela estarán bien", dijo en una entrevista la semana pasada. Según Welligence Energy Analytics, se prevé que el despliegue de equipos en Venezuela se centrará principalmente en unidades de reacondicionamiento, destinadas a la reapertura y reparación de pozos en campos maduros, hasta finales de 2027. Sumado a los planes de expansión de las grandes petroleras, este enfoque elevaría la producción de crudo a cerca de 1,5 millones de barriles por día (bpd) para finales de 2027, frente a los 1,2 millones de bpd actuales, señaló la consultora. "Mantenemos un optimismo cauteloso", afirmó Andrés Armijos, director de Welligence para América Latina, en referencia al plan de inversiones y a las recientes ofertas de empleo. "En realidad, esto llevará tiempo".

item.title: First-ever TGL trade sends The Bay's Shane Lowry to Boston
item.description: Ireland's Shane Lowry moved from The Bay Golf Club to Boston Common Golf in the first trade in TGL history on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ireland's Shane Lowry moved from The Bay Golf Club to Boston Common Golf in the first trade in TGL history on Monday. Lowry, winner of The Open Championship in 2019, joins good friend Rory McIlroy of Northern Ireland in Boston's lineup. In exchange, The Bay acquired Boston's fourth selection to fill its open roster slot this season. The Bay also receives one future selection over the next three offseasons plus additional "commercial considerations," the league said. The move comes as TGL expands to five-player rosters for the 2027 season. Boston Common opens the season on Jan. 2 against Los Angeles Golf Club. "I'm delighted to be joining Boston Common Golf," Lowry said in a statement. "Having Rory alongside me and being part of this group makes it particularly exciting, and I'm looking forward to helping the team bring a championship to Boston." Boston's roster last season featured McIlroy, Keegan Bradley, Australia's Adam Scott and Japan's Hideki Matsuyama. "Shane is a fierce competitor with a tremendous all-around game, and I'm excited to have him on our side," Bradley said. "He brings the kind of energy that makes team golf fun, and he'll fit right in with this group. We're eager to get back to SoFi Center, and adding Shane gives us even more confidence as we chase a championship for Boston." Lowry, 39, recorded his most recent professional win at the Irish Open last month on the DP World Tour. The remaining members for The Bay Golf Club are Wyndham Clark, Sweden's Ludvig Aberg and Australia's Min Woo Lee. "Shane helped build The Bay Golf Club from day one -- in the team room, on the course and with our fans and partners," said Eric Kwait, The Bay's team president. "He's a major champion, and one of the most genuine and beloved players in professional golf, and he'll always be part of our story. We wish Shane and his family nothing but success in the future." --Field Level Media

item.title: Venezuela oilfield hiring picks up as first wave of investment builds
item.description: Oilfield service companies including Weatherford International , Baker Hughes , Halliburton and SLB are advertising dozens of jobs in Venezuela, according to company websites, an early sign that a Washington-backed plan to rebuild the country's energy industry is gaining traction.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney, Marianna Parraga
item.content:encoded: Oilfield service companies including Weatherford International (WFRD.O) , Baker Hughes (BKR.O) , Halliburton (HAL.N) and SLB (SLB.N) are advertising dozens of jobs in Venezuela, according to company websites, an early sign that a Washington-backed plan to rebuild the country's energy industry is gaining traction. The hiring could help reverse a sanctions-era exodus of companies and professionals from the country and comes as the administration of US President Donald Trump pushes a $100 billion oil revival plan following the capture of then-President Nicolas Maduro in January. With some major producers signaling they need political stability and clear legal rules before committing big money, international oil service firms are taking initial steps to put workers, rigs and equipment on the ground. Weatherford, which had scaled back its presence in Venezuela in 2019, has at least 20 open positions, mostly for the oil and gas hubs of Anaco and Maturin, which it started advertising last month. The firm is seeking operation supervisors, drilling specialists and engineers, the company's career website page showed. The US company is set to host a ceremony with Eni (ENI.MI) this month, a source said, following an [USN:L1N44U0HI TEXT:"agreement"] with state-run PDVSA in September for the Italian producer to expand at Venezuela's Orinoco Belt. Eni has engaged Weatherford to help increase production, the source said. Weatherford and Eni did not reply to requests for comment. Venezuela has the world's largest oil reserves, but it pumps only about 1.2 million barrels per day (bpd), a fraction of what those reserves could support. Baker Hughes, which also is expanding in the country, has a dozen openings on its website, posting roles in Maracaibo — Venezuela's second-largest oil region. The company signed an agreement this month with PDVSA, engineering firm Lindsayca and developer Fulcrum LNG to reactivate gas infrastructure. SLB, meanwhile, has 35 vacancies on its website for positions in Anaco, Maturin and Caracas, with postings dating back around six months. Halliburton said in early October it was seeking to expand the company's talent network in Venezuela. A Baker Hughes spokesperson said the company does not comment on personnel. SLB declined to comment. Halliburton did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Most foreign oil service firms had shut down or reduced operations in Venezuela following US sanctions in 2019, laying off or transferring staff and removing equipment from the country. RIGS ON THE WAY Equipment is starting to return, though from a low base. Only two drilling rigs were active in Venezuela this month, according to Baker Hughes data. US-backed North American Blue Energy Partners said it received two drilling units last week, and Chevron is expected to soon [USN:L6N4500X7 TEXT:"activate"] four. One of the largest US land drilling contractors, Patterson-UTI (PTEN.O) , said it is currently shipping components for 10 older rigs of a type CEO Andy Hendricks said the company has not used in the US in about 15 years. "It'll be fine for Venezuela," he said in an interview last week. Through the end of next year, deployments are expected to focus mostly on workover rigs to reopen and repair wells at mature fields, according to Welligence Energy Analytics. Combined with major oil firms' expansion plans, that approach would help lift crude output to some 1.5 million bpd by late 2027 from the 1.2 million bpd now, the consultancy said. "We are being cautiously optimistic," said Andres Armijos, Welligence's head for Latin America, referring to the investment plan and recent job postings. "In reality, this will take time."

item.title: Kansas adds NBA draft pick Trey Kaufman-Renn to roster
item.description: Trey Kaufman-Renn, the 59th overall pick by Minnesota in the 2026 NBA Draft in June, is officially on the Kansas roster as he seeks a sixth year of eligibility.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Trey Kaufman-Renn, the 59th overall pick by Minnesota in the 2026 NBA Draft in June, is officially on the Kansas roster as he seeks a sixth year of eligibility. Kaufman-Renn, 24, never signed a pro contract with the Timberwolves. As a second-round pick, contract agreements are not guaranteed in the NBA. Last season, the 6-foot-9 forward averaged 14.2 points, 8.3 rebounds and 2.5 assists in 37 starts at Purdue. Kaufman-Renn began practicing with the Jayhawks last week and received a temporary injunction to participate while hoping for another year of eligibility. He would take the roster spot of Grant Mordini, a freshman guard who suffered a season-ending patellar tendon injury in September. "Trey Kaufman-Renn, who had a tremendous career at Purdue, has enrolled in classes, and is practicing with us as of Sunday," Kansas coach Bill Self said. "He reached the national championship game, the Elite Eight and the Sweet 16 at Purdue and has been extremely well-drilled and well-coached. Even though it's late in the process, because of his basketball IQ, we think his transition will be quicker than most put in the same circumstance." The Jayhawks open the regular season at home against Fordham on Nov. 2. Kaufman-Renn played in 147 games (112 starts) over four seasons with the Boilermakers, averaging 11.3 points, 5.2 rebounds and 1.6 assists. He redshirted his first year on campus and was a first-team All-Big Ten selection in 2024-25. --Field Level Media

item.title: Solvay abaisse ses objectifs annuels, le conflit au Moyen-Orient pèse
item.description: Solvay a abaissé lundi ses objectifs pour l'ensemble de l'année 2026, le groupe chimique belge prenant acte du fait que le conflit au Moyen-Orient et l'arrêt d'une usine de peroxyde en Arabie saoudite ont pesé sur ses résultats du seul troisième trimestre.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Solvay (SOLB.BR) a abaissé lundi ses objectifs pour l'ensemble de l'année 2026, le groupe chimique belge prenant acte du fait que le conflit au Moyen-Orient et l'arrêt d'une usine de peroxyde en Arabie saoudite ont pesé sur ses résultats du seul troisième trimestre. • L'entreprise table désormais sur un Ebitda (bénéfice avant intérêts, impôts, dépréciation et amortissement) annuel compris entre 720 et 740 millions d'euros et un flux de trésorerie disponible situé entre 120 et 150 millions d'euros. • Le groupe anticipait précédemment un Ebitda sous-jacent compris entre 770 et 850 millions d'euros en 2026, et un flux de trésorerie d'au moins 200 millions d'euros. • Le conflit au Moyen-Orient a eu un impact négatif d’environ 25 millions d'euros sur l’Ebitda sous-jacent au troisième trimestre, selon un communiqué du groupe. • L'arrêt prolongé de l'usine Peroxides dans le complexe de Sadara à Jubail, en Arabie saoudite, a impacté le trimestre. • Le groupe a enregistré sur la période un chiffre d’affaires net sous-jacent de 1,03 milliard d'euros, un Ebitda sous-jacent de 173 millions d'euros, et un flux de trésorerie aux actionnaires de Solvay des activités poursuivies de 54 millions d'euros. • En raison de la "quiet period" en cours, Solvay ne fera pas d’autres commentaires avant la publication de ses résultats complets du troisième trimestre, le 4 novembre, précise le communiqué.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS L'Europe finit dans le rouge, pénalisée par les tensions après les événements en France
item.description: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en nette baisse lundi, face aux craintes d'instabilité politique et financière en France à la suite des scènes de chaos en marge de la mobilisation nationale de samedi contre la vie chère.
item.dc:creator: Coralie Lamarque
item.content:encoded: Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en nette baisse lundi, face aux craintes d'instabilité politique et financière en France à la suite des scènes de chaos en marge de la mobilisation nationale de samedi contre la vie chère. À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) a perdu 1,11% à 7.868,05 points. À Francfort, le Dax (.GDAXI) a lâché 1,18% et à Londres, le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) a cédé 1,08%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) a reculé de 0,96%, le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) de 0,83% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) de 0,80%. Les inquiétudes à la suite des pillages et des violences dans plusieurs villes en France, en marge des manifestations menées samedi contre la vie chère, se répercutent sur les marchés financiers européens, en attisant les craintes concernant la situation politique et financière de la deuxième économie du bloc européen. Alors que les investisseurs étaient déjà préoccupés par le niveau de la dette publique française et le devenir du projet de budget 2027 actuellement débattu par les parlementaires, la tournure des évènements du week-end jette une nouvelle ombre sur la stabilité politique française auprès des opérateurs. Le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, a présenté lundi sa démission, s'estimant "responsable de tout ce qui se passe", tandis que le président Emmanuel Macron l'a rejetée. Le Premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, a déclaré pour sa part avoir donné instruction aux préfets d'instaurer des couvre-feux partiels et localisés, à la suite des violences et des pillages en marge de la mobilisation de samedi qui mêlait revendications des lycéens et mécontentement contre la vie chère. Sébastien Lecornu a jugé qu'un recours à l'état d'urgence n'était pas d'actualité mais restait envisageable, tout en martelant sa détermination à "rétablir l'ordre". Les tensions politiques exacerbent le marché de la dette souveraine française, l'écart entre les obligations allemandes et françaises à 10 ans se creusant à 147 points de base. "Six mois supplémentaires de vide politique représentent une période particulièrement longue pour les marchés, l’économie et les entrepreneurs", a déclaré Kevin Thozet, membre du comité d'investissement de Carmignac, dans une note. VALEURS À Paris, alors que la plupart des valeurs du SBF 120 (.SBF120) ont fini dans le rouge, Rubis (RUBF.PA) a gagné 2,6% après avoir annoncé [USN:L8N46505D TEXT:"lundi"] un projet de transformation en société anonyme dotée d’un directoire et d’un conseil de surveillance. Les craintes politiques en France ont particulièrement pénalisé les banques, Crédit Agricole (CAGR.PA) et BNP (BNPP.PA) ayant reculé respectivement 2,64% et 2,48%. Lanterne rouge du CAC 40, Société Générale (SOGN.PA) a perdu 3,41%. À WALL STREET À l'heure de la clôture en Europe, Wall Street évolue dans le vert. Le Dow Jones (.DJI) se retourne à la hausse et gagne 0,17%, tandis que le Standard & Poor's 500 (.SPX) avance de 0,86% et le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) progresse de 1,73%. LES INDICATEURS DU JOUR Aucun indicateur majeur n'était à l'agenda de lundi. CHANGES La devise européenne subit les inquiétudes exacerbées concernant la situation budgétaire en France, la deuxième économie du bloc monétaire. L'euro perd 0,27% à 1,1209 dollar , tandis que le dollar gagne 0,14% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) . TAUX Le marché obligataire français est [USN:L8N4650B8 TEXT:"impacté"] par les craintes d'instabilité politique et financière attisées par les scènes de chaos observées ce week-end en marge de la mobilisation nationale. Le rendement de l'OAT à dix ans s'est établi à 4,9291%. Le deux ans a atteint 3,6479%. Le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans a terminé à 3,4540% et le deux ans à 3,0920%. Le rendement des Treasuries à dix ans avance de 3,8 points de base à 5,1355%. Le deux ans gagne 3,4 points de base à 4,7698%. PÉTROLE Les cours pétroliers reculent légèrement, les investisseurs évaluant l'impact des dérogations accordées par les États-Unis concernant certaines sanctions et certains droits de douane pesant sur les exportations russes. Le Brent cède 0,64% à 109,16 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) lâche 0,11% à 101,52 dollars. item.title: Christiane Amanpour to leave CNN after four decades as Ellison era begins

item.content:encoded: CNN chief international anchor Christiane Amanpour will leave next year, after 43 years with the network, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters on Monday. The news channel has recently come under the ownership of Skydance (SKYD.N) , whose CEO David Ellison has faced criticism over his stewardship of CBS News. Amanpour will end her daily shows across CNN and PBS at the end of this year She will continue to host a weekly show on CNN through May and work on a transition through June Amanpour, whose first major assignment was covering the first Gulf War, went on to report on conflicts in Bosnia, Rwanda, Afghanistan, Ukraine and Iran Skydance, formerly Paramount Skydance, completed its [USN:L4N45S0XK TEXT:"$110 billion takeover"] of Warner Bros Discovery earlier this month, bringing CNN and CBS News under one roof CNN chief Mark Thompson and CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss [USN:L6N45R0R0 TEXT:"kept their roles"], with both reporting to Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz Lawmakers have criticized Ellison for [USN:L1N43G10Q TEXT:"tailoring news coverage"] at CBS News to favor President Donald Trump

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brasil detectó un caso de enfermedad de Newcastle en una granja de pavos del estado sureño de Santa Catarina, informó el lunes el ministro de Agricultura, André de Paula, quien añadió que se habían puesto en marcha medidas sanitarias que afectarían a 133 granjas de la región. La enfermedad de Newcastle es altamente contagiosa y afecta a las aves, al igual que la gripe aviar. Brasil es el mayor exportador mundial de carne de pollo. Las autoridades brasileñas dijeron que están elaborando informes detallados y que compartirían toda la información relevante con los principales socios comerciales del país. El secretario interino de Comercio Agrícola de Brasil, Rafael Requiao, señaló que es demasiado pronto aún para facilitar información concreta sobre posibles suspensiones de las importaciones. China, uno de los principales destinos de las exportaciones de pollo de Brasil, impuso en 2024 un embargo a la carne de pollo procedente de Rio Grande do Sul tras confirmarse un caso de enfermedad de Newcastle en una granja comercial de ese estado, también del sur del país.

item.title: Israel reanudará los envíos comerciales a Gaza tras la disputa con Hamás sobre cobros
item.description: Israel anunció el lunes que volvería a permitir el envío de mercancías comerciales a Gaza tras una interrupción de varios días a raíz de una disputa fiscal entre Hamás y los comerciantes, restableciendo así una ruta clave para el suministro de alimentos y otros productos de primera necesidad a este enclave, que depende de la ayuda humanitaria.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israel anunció el lunes que volvería a permitir el envío de mercancías comerciales a Gaza tras una interrupción de varios días a raíz de una disputa fiscal entre Hamás y los comerciantes, restableciendo así una ruta clave para el suministro de alimentos y otros productos de primera necesidad a este enclave, que depende de la ayuda humanitaria. La COGAT, la agencia militar israelí encargada de supervisar los asuntos humanitarios en Gaza, dijo que tomó la decisión después de que los comerciantes informaron que las autoridades de Hamás habían retirado la exigencia de pagos de 10.000 shekels (3.225 dólares) por camión. "La reanudación de la coordinación se está llevando a cabo de conformidad con el compromiso de Israel con las disposiciones humanitarias del acuerdo de alto el fuego", afirmó. La COGAT señaló que los informes de los comerciantes no se habían verificado de forma independiente y que los envíos se reanudarían de forma gradual, dando prioridad a los productos de primera necesidad de cara al invierno. Se reforzará la supervisión para garantizar que los pagos se realicen y se reciban únicamente a través de transferencias bancarias documentadas, y cualquier comerciante del que se compruebe que ha pagado a Hamás se enfrentará a la exclusión del sistema. Hamás afirmó que la cuota de 10.000 shekels era una contribución voluntaria de los habitantes de Gaza con mayor poder adquisitivo a un fondo nacional destinado a apoyar a las personas necesitadas en el territorio devastado por la guerra. La mayoría de los habitantes de Gaza siguen dependiendo de la ayuda luego de tres años de guerra, desplazamientos repetidos y severas restricciones en el envío de ayuda. Aunque el alto el fuego negociado por Estados Unidos el año pasado detuvo los combates más intensos, no ha puesto fin a los ataques israelíes. Las autoridades sanitarias locales dijeron el lunes que al menos cinco palestinos, entre ellos un niño de 14 años, murieron en distintos ataques israelíes en la ciudad de Gaza y en Jan Yunis. El Ejército israelí no hizo comentarios de inmediato. Israel dice que Hamás ha seguido rearmándose y llevando a cabo ataques en violación del alto el fuego, mientras que Hamás acusa a Israel de socavar el acuerdo. Las autoridades sanitarias de Gaza dicen que unos 1.500 palestinos han perdido la vida a causa de los disparos israelíes desde el alto el fuego de octubre de 2025, mientras que Israel afirma que cuatro de sus soldados han sido asesinados por militantes en Gaza durante el mismo periodo. (1 dólar = 3,0991 shekels)

item.title: Trump administration cannot overhaul fair housing grant program, appeals court rules
item.description: A federal appeals court on Monday refused to allow President Donald Trump's administration to redirect money away from over 100 non-profit organizations that had historically received funding to help prevent and investigate housing discrimination.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A federal appeals court on Monday refused to allow President Donald Trump's administration to redirect money away from over 100 non-profit organizations that had historically received funding to help prevent and investigate housing discrimination. The Boston-based 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals largely rejected the administration's request to lift an order by a lower-court judge who had blocked the US Department of Housing and Urban Development from implementing sweeping changes to a decades-old grant program designed to combat housing discrimination. Boston-based US District Judge Myong Joun had [USN:L1N44N107 TEXT:"sided in August "]with the National Fair Housing Alliance and the Massachusetts Fair Housing Center, which sued in July to block what they said was the latest effort by HUD under Trump to roll back fair housing enforcement. A three-judge 1st Circuit panel comprised only of appointees of Democratic presidents said the Trump administration had failed to demonstrate it was likely to succeed in finding that Joun exceeded his authority by issuing that decision. The court declined to put most of Joun's decision on hold while the government pursues its appeal. It agreed to lift one part requiring HUD to issue new notices of funding opportunities for fiscal year 2025 that would require grants to be awarded under the 2024 system. Joun imposed that condition at a time when the funding was rapidly set to expire on September 30. But the administration said that after he ruled, the basis for that part of Joun's decision was eliminated when Congress through a funding measure effectively extended the expiration date to September 30, 2027. HUD and lawyers for the plaintiffs did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The case centers on the Fair Housing Initiatives Program, which Congress created in 1987 and that has long provided multi-year grants for fair housing organizations to help enforce the Fair Housing Act. In the past, HUD would typically award over 100 grants ranging from $75,000 to $425,000, according to lawyers for the fair housing groups. That funding supported a network of organizations that assist people claiming they experienced housing discrimination. In July, HUD moved to overhaul that system by announcing it would not allocate any of its congressionally appropriated funding for the 2025 fiscal year to private enforcement initiatives or to multi-year grants issued through the Fair Housing Initiatives Program. HUD instead planned to use $46 million of the $56 million that Congress had appropriated for just five grants, $25 million of which would go to a law school. The remaining $10 million could go to a state or local agency. The Trump administration also sought to force grant recipients to sign onto unrelated conditions to receive funding, by imposing requirements that they not use any funding to support "gender ideology" or "illegal immigration." Joun, an appointee of Democratic President Joe Biden, said HUD failed to provide a reasoned explanation or rely on relevant data in crafting the restructuring, which "effectively bars the very housing organizations that have been effectuating FHIP's mission year after year since its enactment." The Trump administration swiftly appealed, contending HUD had discretion to decide how to allocate the funds and that the judge "had no basis whatsoever to dictate how HUD should disburse the funds in question." "The orders micromanage HUD’s administration of a national program and prevent HUD from exercising the discretion that Congress gave it," the US Department of Justice argued on the administration's behalf. Massachusetts Fair Housing Center, et al v. Department of Housing and Urban Development, et al, 1st Circuit, No. 26-2084. For the plaintiffs: Lila Miller of Relman Colfax For HUD: Sarah Clark Griffin of the US Department of Justice Read more: [USN:L1N44N107 TEXT:"US judge blocks Trump overhaul of funding for fair housing groups"]

item.title: Top hyperscalers likely to have more AI-linked debt than now known, S&P Global warns
item.description: S&P Global estimates the world's biggest tech firms are likely to have more AI-linked liabilities than currently known, although its top analyst for the sector sees no need to change any ratings at present.
item.dc:creator: Marc Jones
item.content:encoded: S&P Global estimates the world's biggest tech firms are likely to have more AI-linked liabilities than currently known, although its top analyst for the sector sees no need to change any ratings at present. Debt issued by AI infrastructure providers and so-called 'neocloud' firms such as Nvidia-backed CoreWeave has sunk to [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"increasingly stressed levels"] in recent weeks amid concerns about the aggressive scale of their borrowing. S&P's Global Head for Digital Infrastructure Mark Habib said the biggest risk to hyperscalers' ratings remained whether expected profits fail to materialise. But he also highlighted so-called 'interconnected financing structures', where hyperscalers effectively guarantee huge data centre builds, or smaller AI companies. "It is safe to assume that there is more (debt) out there that we are not seeing," Habib said during a roundtable in London. "If it's not reported, then it's not part of the disclosure by the hyperscalers. Also, if we are not rating the transactions where this liability may accrue, then the fact of the matter is that we might not have the visibility." S&P expects the top six US hyperscalers — Amazon (AMZN.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Oracle (ORCL.N) , Meta (META.O) , and SpaceX (SPCX.O) — to spend more than $7 trillion on data centers and other AI-related capex between 2025 and 2030, and have negative free cash flow until at least next year. Habib said there wasn't an estimate of how much additional debt the circular financing might add to firms' balance sheets, although he said S&P was trying to take a "holistic" view overall. Back in July, it downgraded Oracle to BBB-, the lowest rung of 'investment grade', on concerns about its AI spending and what it called "an uncertain path to profitability". Habib was also asked whether the recent market selloff of bonds linked to the aggressive AI buildout was a sign that investors see them as riskier than ratings indicate. "For now, we don't have the view that there is a major disconnect that needs to force our ratings to change at this point," he said, saying S&P's scores were designed to take a longer-term view. He said what could change that view was if it became clear the amount of money being spent was no longer sustainable. "And that could come from a variety of drivers," Habib said. "Further increases in the investments (by AI firms), or a view that the revenue rate of competition is getting too intense."

item.title: Tennis Elina Svitolina annonce se séparer de Gaël Monfils, invoquant les conséquences de la guerre
item.description: Elina Svitolina, sixième joueuse mondiale de tennis, a annoncé lundi se séparer du Français Gaël Monfils, ancien numéro six mondial du circuit ATP, l'Ukrainienne précisant que le poids émotionnel de la guerre menée par la Russie contre son pays natal l'avait amenée à ressentir le besoin de se redécouvrir.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Elina Svitolina, sixième joueuse mondiale de tennis, a annoncé lundi se séparer du Français Gaël Monfils, ancien numéro six mondial du circuit ATP, l'Ukrainienne précisant que le poids émotionnel de la guerre menée par la Russie contre son pays natal l'avait amenée à ressentir le besoin de se redécouvrir. Le couple s'était marié en juillet 2021 et leur fille avait Skai est née en octobre 2022. Annonçant cette séparation dans un post Instagram, Elina Svitolina a décrit les difficultés personnelles auxquelles elle a été confrontée depuis l'invasion de l(Ukraine par la Russie en février 2022. "C'est la chose la plus difficile que j’aie jamais eu à partager. Tout le monde sait à quel point l’Ukraine compte pour moi. Ce dont j’ai rarement parlé, c’est de ce que la guerre m’a fait vivre intérieurement". "L'année dernière, je vous avais dit que je devais m’éloigner des courts parce que je n’étais pas dans le bon état d’esprit. Aujourd’hui, je souhaite m’ouvrir un peu davantage. Ce que vous n’avez pas vu, ce sont les nuits blanches, les doutes et le sentiment de me perdre peu à peu". "Gaël a tout vu. Il n’a jamais lâché ma main. Nous nous sommes battus ensemble pendant longtemps, de toutes nos forces. Mais certaines batailles se livrent au plus profond de soi, et aucun amour, aussi grand soit-il, ne peut les remporter à votre place." Elina Svitolina, 32 ans, a demandé de la bienveillance et le respect de sa vie privée alors que sa famille traverse cette séparation, soulignant que personne n'était à blâmer. "Avec le temps, j’ai fini par comprendre que je devais retrouver le chemin vers moi-même et que je ne pouvais pas y parvenir au sein de notre mariage", a-t-elle ajouté. "C’est la vérité la plus difficile à laquelle j’ai jamais dû faire face et la chose la plus difficile que j’ai jamais dû dire à la personne que j’aime." "Gaël m’a écoutée. Il a respecté mes besoins avec une force et une dignité que je n’oublierai jamais. Gaël m’a aimée dans mes plus grandes joies comme dans mes moments les plus sombres, et je l’ai aimé de tout mon cœur". "Skai passera toujours en premier. Notre mariage prend fin, mais pas notre famille. Nous serons toujours ses parents, côte à côte, à chaque étape de sa vie". Sur le court, Elina Svitolina, quadruple demi-finaliste de Grand Chelem, s’est récemment qualifiée pour les finales WTA de fin de saison à Indian Wells, en Californie. Le Français Gael Monfils, 40 ans, l’un des joueurs les plus charismatiques de sa génération, a [USN:L6N3VI0EM TEXT:"pris sa retraite du tennis professionnel"], selon l’Agence internationale pour l’intégrité du tennis (ITIA). Il prévoyait de prendre sa retraite fin 2026 et de faire ses adieux lors du Masters de Paris en novembre, mais l’ITIA le répertorie désormais comme retraité.

item.title: Líder de secta en Kenia que imponía ayuno extremo es declarado culpable matar a 191 niños
item.description: Un tribunal de Kenia declaró el lunes culpable al líder de la secta de la inanición, Paul Mackenzie, y a otras 30 personas, de asesinato, por la muerte de 190 niños y un adulto en uno de los peores desastres relacionados con sectas de la historia reciente.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Un tribunal de Kenia declaró el lunes culpable al líder de la secta de la inanición, Paul Mackenzie, y a otras 30 personas, de asesinato, por la muerte de 190 niños y un adulto en uno de los peores desastres relacionados con sectas de la historia reciente. Mackenzie fue detenido en 2023 tras una denuncia recibida por la policía, y semanas más tarde las autoridades comenzaron a hallar cadáveres en fosas comunes en el bosque de Shakahola, cerca de la costa del sureste de Kenia. La fiscalía acusó a Mackenzie y su Iglesia Internacional de las Buenas Nuevas de organizar una secta cristiana apocalíptica en la que ordenaban a sus seguidores que se dejaran morir de hambre a sí mismos y a sus hijos para ir al cielo antes del fin del mundo. Mackenzie negó los cargos de asesinato, alegando que no obligó a las víctimas a morir de hambre, pero el tribunal rechazó el argumento. En total, se han recuperado más de 400 cadáveres del bosque de Shakahola. Muchos se encontraban en avanzado estado de descomposición, por lo que solo se pudieron identificar 26 cadáveres. La sentencia del lunes abarcó 191 fallecimientos, mientras que las investigaciones sobre las demás muertes siguen abiertas. FAMILIAS ESCUCHAN EL VEREDICTO EN EL TRIBUNAL La jueza Diana Kavedza Mochache dijo en una vista, que duró más de ocho horas, que, en algunos casos, se aisló a los niños y se les negó la comida mientras sus padres observaban. Mackenzie se encontraba en la sala, vestido con una camiseta a rayas y pantalones rojos, sentado junto a su esposa, que también está acusada. Permaneció en silencio, con la mirada perdida, antes de que se dictara la sentencia. Los familiares de algunas de las personas que fallecieron en el bosque se reunieron para escuchar la sentencia en el Tribunal Superior de Mombasa. Francis Wanje, de 62 años, perdió a ocho familiares, entre ellos dos nietos, a manos de la secta. "Ha sido algo realmente duro para nosotros como familia, y nos ha afectado mucho en términos de problemas psicológicos (...) Estaba esperando este día", dijo antes de la audiencia. La tragedia de Shakahola ha conmocionado a Kenia desde el descubrimiento de fosas comunes en el bosque costero hace más de tres años. Personas con conocimiento directo de las actividades de la secta explicaron a Reuters que Mackenzie planeó la inanición masiva en tres fases: primero los niños, luego las mujeres y los jóvenes, y finalmente el resto de los hombres. Mackenzie, un antiguo taxista, prohibió a los miembros de la secta enviar a sus hijos al colegio y acudir al hospital cuando estaban enfermos, tachando a dichas instituciones de satánicas, contaron algunos de sus seguidores a Reuters en 2023.

item.title: How the gold boom is fuelling tree loss from Ghana to the Amazon
item.description: As the price of gold booms, so does the roar of excavators and scream of chainsaws in some of the world’s most ecologically sensitive forests.
item.dc:creator: Mark Hillsdon
item.content:encoded: As the price of gold booms, so does the roar of excavators and scream of chainsaws in some of the world’s most ecologically sensitive forests. Between 2001 and 2019, gold drove more deforestation than any other mineral, from the dense tropical forests of the Amazon and Africa’s western coast, to the boreal forests of Russia, and down through Myanmar and Indonesia. But with prices having spiked more than 120% in the last five years, fuelled by geopolitical instability and disruptions to international trade, campaigners fear the gold rush has only accelerated, with huge implications for the world’s forests. “The rapid rise in the price of gold creates a powerful economic incentive for mining expansion,” explains Andres Santana, senior manager for combating illegal deforestation at Amazon Conservation, in an email. “Higher prices increase the potential returns from extracting gold, including from remote and environmentally sensitive areas, adding further pressure to forests and local communities.” Criminal gangs have moved in as gold’s price has risen, funding illegal mining and taking advantage of gold’s mercurial properties; it’s ability to be re-smelted creates a shape-shifting currency that is hard to trace, and easy to launder. As Reuters has reported , gold smuggling out of Africa has surged over the past decade, finding its way onto international markets through regional hubs in Mali, and less regulated markets in Dubai, Istanbul and Mumbai. It’s these loopholes that campaigners want the industry to close. Hannah Mowat, campaigns coordinator at the environmental NGO Fern, says in an email that in many countries “small-scale illicit mining is largely controlled by big players, who operate with foreign money and have top political connections. These are not artisanal miners panning for gold – these are highly mechanised, highly financialised and connected actors.” A specialist handles ingots of 99.99% pure gold. The price of gold has spiked more than 120% in the last five years, fuelled by geopolitical instability and trade disruptions. REUTERS/Alexander Manzyuk Not only does this illicit mining cause deforestation, but the use of mercury and cyanide poisons water supplies and food chains, leading to severe health consequences for communities living downstream of mining sites. On a recent visit to Ghana, Jonathan Byers, a consultant and geospatial analyst at the environmental NGO Mighty Earth saw entire river valleys where the water flowed milky brown due to pollution from gold mining. “They can’t even put (it) on the cocoa trees anymore because it kills them,” he explains. “It is the human impacts of this that are pretty catastrophic.” While industrial gold mining has been linked with harm to communities through deforestation and pollution , major international mining companies must comply with strict rules to be members of organisations such as the World Gold Council (WGC), whose Responsible Gold Mining Principles sets a framework for the gold supply chain, including investors and consumers. Another initiative is the Gold Bar Integrity (GBI) programme, run jointly by the WGC and the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA). It uses blockchain technology to digitally trace gold as it moves through global supply chains, with refineries having to report the country of origin for every gram of gold they take in, explains Neil Harby, LBMA's chief technical officer. Applying the so-called alchemy test, he says, “means a refinery cannot … produce more gold bars than the gold it sourced”. Around 90% of industrially mined gold (sanctions mean Russia is excluded) are covered by the GBI, but the standard only takes in a small fraction of gold from artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM), even though this accounts for as much as 20% of global production. While not all ASGM gold is illegal, “this is where the deforestation is happening,” says Harby. The rising price of gold has also increased the demand for scrap and recycled gold, says Harby, which now makes up as much as 50% of the gold market. The link between recycled and ASGM gold is strong, he says. “It (ASGM gold) gets passed as recycled gold; it loses its identity, what we call ‘gold-washing’.” Chemically finger-printing the gold can help. “Gold from certain countries has certain signatures,” says Harby, “but, as this gold is re-smelted time and time again, it becomes increasingly difficult to track these trace elements.” Jewellery made from gold is smelted down at a factory. The rising price of gold has increased the demand for recycled gold, which now makes up as much as 50% of the gold market. REUTERS/Vasily Fedosenko Ghana is suffering more than most from illicit mining, and is now one of the most heavily mined countries in the world. In 2022, the then government passed legislation opening up nearly 90% of the country’s 9 million hectares of forest reserves to mining. One study found a 5.9% decline in forest cover in one reserve, which had experienced a 19-fold increase in mining, and a complete absence of vegetation in areas that were heavily mine. This led to the creation of the Ghana Coalition Against Galamsey, explains Daryl Bosu, deputy director at the conservation NGO A Roche Ghana. Galamsey roughly translates as “gather and sell”, he says, when historically people could pick gold nuggets from riverbeds or fields after heavy rainfall. In 2025 a new government repealed the law but Bosu says the reality on the ground is unchanged. “Our forests reserves are still under rampage and destruction by illegal miners.” Last year the Ghanian government set up the Gold Board (Goldbod) to clamp down on criminal gangs who were smuggling gold out of Ghana. But the system doesn’t address traceability, says Bosu. He has no doubt that gold linked to deforestation in Ghana continues to reach London markets (which account for 70% of global trade). He wants a zero-tolerance approach towards miners and politicians involved in illegal mining, and in this respect can see a glimmer of hope. In July, politician and businessman politician Bernard Antwi Boasiako was jailed for 20 years for involvement in illegal mining. At the same time, Ghana and the WGC signed an agreement to accelerate the formalisation of the country’s ASGM sector, with a mixture of investment and training. Another area on the frontline of expanding gold mining is the Amazon. According to March’s inaugural report of the Amazon Mining Watch Panorama, in the last quarter of 2025 there was an estimated 6,000 ha of new mining-related deforestation (MRD) across the Amazon Basin, much of it put down to the quest for gold. A cocoa farmer, visits her cocoa plantation destroyed by illegal gold mining in the Samreboi community in the Western Region, Ghana, February 26, 2024. REUTERS/Francis Kokoroko Amazon Mining Watch is a platform led by Amazon Conservation, Earth Genome and the Pulitzer Center. The report used AI to analyse mining scars across all nine Amazonian countries, and showed that as well as new incursions in areas such as Territorio Charip in Ecuador, there was a resurgence of activity in the Igarapes do Juruena State Park in Brazil, where MRD rose by 660% between August 2025 and April 2026. A further 200 ha of MRD were detected in Peru’s Tambopata National Reserve, which had seen levels of forest destruction drop after a major government operation. “Criminal organisations can exploit weak… gold traceability systems and gaps in due diligence requirements to introduce illegally extracted gold into legal supply chains,” says Amazon Conservation’s Santana, “taking advantage of the Amazon’s vast geography, institutional weaknesses and limited regional coordination.” Amazon Conservation has also launched the Amazon Mining Policy Scoreboard, which evaluates and compares the legal and policy frameworks governing gold mining across the Amazon. It shows that many countries have strong legal frameworks on paper, but implementation lags, with governments failing to address the underlying drivers of illegal mining, as well as providing alternative livelihoods for communities. Victoire Girard, a professor at the Nova School of Business and Economics at the New University of Lisbon, says illegal mining provides a livelihood for millions of people, which means a simple ban on illicit gold mining won’t work. An illegal wildcat gold mine in an area of deforested Amazon rainforest in Para State, Brazil. REUTERS/Nacho Doce “People are attracted to gold mining because they can’t do anything else,” she explains. “If there’s a drought and cultivators lose everything, they’re going to turn to gold as an alternative livelihood.” There’s already a growing trend in Ghana for farmers to grub up their uneconomic cocoa plantations and mine the land instead, she says. To keep the farmers working the land rather than mining it, she believes, companies and governments need to look at issues such as crop insurance and affordable loans. Mowat of FERN agrees there will always be some form of mining, and that communities “must get increased income and wealth from the gold that they are digging out”. This includes having a greater say in the allocation of mining permits, more community benefits and better training of artisanal miners. The WGC also recognises the problem. The council’s global head of public policy, Andrew Naylor, said in an email that while governments have the primary responsibility to enforce laws and improve governance industry and civil society can help by building formal pathways for legitimate ASGM gold to enter the market. “Enforcement is necessary to disrupt criminal networks, but formalisation is what helps prevent them from returning,” he adds. Mowat acknowledges the work that organisations such as the WGC are doing, but points out that its rules are voluntary, and there’s no external scrutiny. In December, London hosts the Illicit Finance Summit, when FERN and other civil society organisations will present a roadmap to address illegal mining’s root causes. Alongside tackling the systemic poverty driving small-scale miners into illicit supply chains, it will also encourage financial centres to do more to ensure that illegal gold can’t be co-mingled with legitimate gold and enter the international financial system. “Unless there is a clear, international standard for responsible gold, that requires market players to know where the gold they are dealing with comes from, then western markets will continue to drive illicit gold mining, and fuel global insecurity, human rights abuses and environmental harm,” Mowat adds.
